key_reasoning.reason: Conversation.update() persistence contract was overridden (required keyword-only columns=, targeted UPDATE with no pre-read, stale-row detection, unlisted-change guard). Call sites then moved over in 3 routers (admin, conversation, feedback) and 4 services (chat naming, checkpoint, conversation, workflow). Base L for several components across layers plus shared utilities, bumped to XL because the change touches a core shared persistence method used by several workflows.

The write path changed for every conversation mutation. If a call site leaves a column out, the change is silently lost. The unlisted-column warning, StaleDataError on rowcount 0 and a history-compat write-back reduce this risk. The pattern is a standard SQLAlchemy core UPDATE with no direct precedent in BaseModelWithSQLSupport. Base M, bumped to L because removing the pre-select is a performance change on a critical path. No security surface is involved.

Diffstat reports 18 files (1368 insertions). That is 9 source files modified across configs/, rest_api/models, rest_api/routers and service/, plus 9 test files. About 3 test files are new (test_conversation_update.py, test_conversation_update_router_sites.py, test_conversation_update_sites.py) and the rest were extended. 16 or more files maps to XXL.

The nearest bundled L example (epmcdme-10401, total 22) matches the band. That example spreads its weight across layers and clarity. This change is concentrated in file count and component fan-out, and it has no schema migration or UI.
